   There's one area that this playoff will negatively effect that no one's talking about. Rivalries. 
  If you have rivalry rematches in the same season/postseason, you'll start to water down great rivalries. I think this is one of the reasons why Conf title games had to go. Imagine the Iron Bowl, then in two weeks later an Iron Bowl rematch for the conf title; then a third Iron Bowl as a playoff matchup.

I don’t understand why the consensus is against a 24 team playoff, I personally think it’s awesome. The issue has never been the amount of teams, but the arbitrary capricious methodology implemented in selecting who is awarded the opportunity to compete for a championship. If they had more automatic qualifiers, I think this 24 playoff system would be perfect and I think it’s the right number of total teams.

There is this wrong notion that it’s going to automatically and implicitly trivialize the value of the regular season. The value of the regular season is much more contingent on the methodology of how teams are selected then the total number of teams as a whole.

There is also a big fat financial incentive that Josh‘s misappropriating whenever ascertaining what the fans actually want. I bet you don’t stop watching the games because of it and that’s what their bottom line number is not forums on your podcast and qualitative based focus groups.

Bottom line, I just strongly disagree that expanding the playoff inherently and categorically diminishes the value of the regular season. That doesn’t make any sense when we’re not putting it up against some sort of objective criteria. The methodology of selecting teams is inherently more significant than the records of the teams themselves, and I don’t know why people don’t understand this.

Your forehead vein is popping out wanting to save something that is already dead. This expansion is what the powers that be hope to use to keep the flies off the corpse a little while longer by generating talk of seeding, home playoff games, and bye weeks. When that novelty wears off, game over. 

Not one single CFB fan I know feels the same about the game, and that has nothing  to do with this expansion. So while your arguments are cogent and well articulated, Pandora’s box was already opened and the obituary has already been written.  People will watch their favorite teams but the days of watching CFB all day Saturday, just for the love of the game, have passed for  the regular fan. 

Just my opinion.

snippet.textDisplay: So, Josh. How is the National Champion determined in College Basketball? Yeah, that's right: Through a now-76-team playoff, wherein ALL 32 conference champions get automatic bids. (There are 363 D-1 Schools, as opposed to 138 FBS schools.) And yes, the champion is determined through a "one-and-done" elimination process -- not unlike earlier football-playoff iterations. My point is simply that the greatly-expanded NCAA Basketball Tournament ("March Madness") is HUGELY popular across the company, with people at offices across the fruited plain filling out brackets - people who know nothing about the teams, the sport, etc., but STILL watch the tournament. So having 24 teams (we should have 40, just like D-3 Football does) will in no way harm the regular season. We should KEEP Conference Championships, and CONTINUE to make them the automatic qualifiers.
